quests.instruction: A concert starts at 7:30 PM. The doors open 45 minutes before the start, and there is a 25-minute queue before the doors open. The journey to the venue takes 35 minutes. What is the latest time to leave home to be in the queue on time?
quests.hint: Work backward: first the doors, then the queue, then the journey.
quests.explanation: The doors open at 6:45 PM. The queue must start at 6:20 PM. Going back 35 minutes for the journey gives 5:45 PM.
quests.funFact: Many venues open their doors an hour or more before a concert begins, so that a large audience can find their seats.

quests.instruction: A relay team has four runners. Each runner takes 4 minutes 30 seconds, and each of the 3 baton changes takes 15 seconds. How long does the relay take in all?
quests.hint: Add all the running time first, then the baton changes.
quests.explanation: 4 × 4 minutes 30 seconds = 18 minutes. Three changes of 15 seconds add 45 seconds. The total is 18 minutes 45 seconds.
quests.funFact: In a relay race, the baton must be passed inside a marked zone that is 20 metres long.

quests.instruction: A pool is open from 6:30 AM to 9:00 PM but closes for cleaning for 1 hour 15 minutes. For how long is it open to swimmers?
quests.hint: Find the whole opening time, then take away the cleaning time.
quests.explanation: 6:30 AM to 9:00 PM is 14 hours 30 minutes. Taking away 1 hour 15 minutes leaves 13 hours 15 minutes.
quests.funFact: The water in a swimming pool is pumped through filters many times every day.

quests.instruction: Rina must get to a match that starts at 4:00 PM. Option A leaves at 3:05 PM and takes 55 minutes in all. Option B leaves at 3:20 PM and takes 45 minutes in all. Option C leaves at 3:10 PM and takes 45 minutes in all. Which option arrives earliest?
quests.hint: Add the journey time to the leaving time for each option.
quests.explanation: Option A arrives at 4:00 PM, Option B arrives at 4:05 PM and Option C arrives at 3:55 PM. So Option C arrives earliest.
quests.funFact: Airlines use computers to compare millions of possible schedules and find the best one.

quests.instruction: Zara has 55 minutes. Plan P: maths 25, reading 20 and tidy-up 15 minutes. Plan Q: maths 25, reading 15 and tidy-up 10 minutes. Plan R: maths 20, reading 20 and tidy-up 20 minutes. Which plan fits into 55 minutes?
quests.hint: Add up the three parts of each plan.
quests.explanation: Plan P and Plan R both take 60 minutes. Plan Q takes 50 minutes, so only Plan Q fits.
quests.funFact: Planners often start with the task that has the earliest deadline.

quests.instruction: School ends at 3:20 PM. Bus 1 leaves at 3:30 and takes 40 minutes. Bus 2 leaves at 3:40 and takes 25 minutes. Bus 3 leaves at 3:45 and takes 30 minutes. Which bus gets a pupil home first?
quests.hint: The bus that leaves first may not arrive first. Find each arrival time.
quests.explanation: Bus 1 arrives at 4:10 PM, Bus 2 arrives at 4:05 PM and Bus 3 arrives at 4:15 PM. So Bus 2 gets the pupil home first.
quests.funFact: Some buses wait at special stops to keep to the timetable. These stops are called timing points.

quests.instruction: A party runs from 2:00 to 5:30 PM. Games take 1 hour 15 minutes, cake takes 25 minutes, and there are two 10-minute breaks. The rest of the time is for a film. How long is the film?
quests.hint: Find the whole party first, then take away everything else.
quests.explanation: 2:00 to 5:30 is 210 minutes. Games, cake and breaks take 75 + 25 + 20 = 120 minutes. 210 − 120 = 90 minutes, which is 1 hour 30 minutes.
quests.funFact: A play in a theatre usually lasts between two and three hours, including the interval.

quests.instruction: 24 pupils each give a 3-minute talk. There is a 1-minute change between talks. How long do the talks take altogether?
quests.hint: How many changes are there between 24 talks?
quests.explanation: 24 talks take 24 × 3 = 72 minutes. There are 23 changes between 24 talks, which add 23 minutes. 72 + 23 = 95 minutes, which is 1 hour 35 minutes.
quests.funFact: A fence with 10 sections needs 11 posts. Counting the gaps and the ends can give different answers, so this is called the fence-post problem.

quests.instruction: Trains run every 12 minutes. The first leaves at 6:00 AM and the last leaves at 7:00 AM. How many trains leave in that time, counting both the first and the last?
quests.hint: List the departure times one by one.
quests.explanation: The trains leave at 6:00, 6:12, 6:24, 6:36, 6:48 and 7:00. That is 6 trains.
quests.funFact: Timetables usually show the first and last services of the day, so passengers know when travel starts and stops.

quests.instruction: City B is 4 hours 30 minutes behind City A. At 8:15 PM in City A, Dev calls his aunt in City B. What time is it for his aunt?
quests.hint: Behind means earlier. Take away 4 hours first, then 30 minutes.
quests.explanation: 8:15 PM minus 4 hours is 4:15 PM. Another 30 minutes back is 3:45 PM.
quests.funFact: There are about 38 different time zone offsets around the world, because some places are half an hour or 45 minutes away from their neighbours.

quests.instruction: A flight leaves City A at 11:40 PM and lasts 6 hours 20 minutes. City B is 4 hours 30 minutes behind City A. What is the local time in City B when the plane lands?
quests.hint: Find the landing time on City A's clock first.
quests.explanation: 11:40 PM plus 6 hours 20 minutes is 6:00 AM on City A's clock. City B is 4 hours 30 minutes behind, so it is 1:30 AM there.
quests.funFact: Astronauts on the International Space Station keep to UTC, one shared time, whichever country they come from.

quests.instruction: A meeting is at 9:00 AM in City B, which is 4 hours 30 minutes behind City A. What time is the meeting in City A?
quests.hint: City A is ahead, so its time is later.
quests.explanation: 9:00 AM plus 4 hours 30 minutes is 1:30 PM.
quests.funFact: Time zone borders are not straight lines. They bend around countries and regions so that places close together share the same time.

quests.instruction: In a year that is not a leap year, a library book is due 28 days after 15 January. What is the due date?
quests.hint: January has 31 days. Count to the end of January first.
quests.explanation: 15 January to 31 January is 16 days. The 12 days that are left reach 12 February.
quests.funFact: Before printing was invented, scribes copied books by hand, and a single book could take months.

quests.instruction: A course meets 5 days a week for 3 hours a day, and it runs for 4 weeks. How many hours is that altogether?
quests.hint: Find the hours in one week first.
quests.explanation: 5 × 3 = 15 hours a week. 4 weeks is 4 × 15 = 60 hours.
quests.funFact: A school year in many countries adds up to roughly 900 to 1,000 hours of lessons.

quests.instruction: A plant is 5 cm tall and grows 2 cm every 3 days. How tall is it after 15 days?
quests.hint: How many 3-day periods are in 15 days?
quests.explanation: 15 days is 5 periods of 3 days. The plant grows 5 × 2 = 10 cm, so it is 5 + 10 = 15 cm tall.
quests.funFact: Most plants grow fastest in warm and sunny weather.

quests.instruction: A classroom clock is 12 minutes fast and shows 8:07. What is the real time?
quests.hint: A fast clock is ahead. Take the extra minutes away.
quests.explanation: The clock is 12 minutes ahead, so the real time is 12 minutes earlier. 8:07 minus 12 minutes is 7:55.
quests.funFact: On a pendulum clock, the clock can be made to run faster or slower by changing the length of the pendulum.

quests.instruction: A watch loses 3 minutes every hour. It is set correctly at 11:00 AM. What does it show when the real time is 3:00 PM?
quests.hint: How many hours pass between 11:00 AM and 3:00 PM?
quests.explanation: 4 hours pass, and the watch loses 4 × 3 = 12 minutes. 3:00 PM minus 12 minutes is 2:48 PM.
quests.funFact: Early mechanical watches could lose around 15 minutes in a single day.

quests.instruction: A timer is set for 45 minutes at 3:20 PM, but it is paused for 6 minutes. When does it ring?
quests.hint: Find the normal ring time first, then add the pause.
quests.explanation: Without the pause it would ring at 4:05 PM. The 6-minute pause pushes it back to 4:11 PM.
quests.funFact: In many sports, a timeout stops the game clock so that no playing time is lost.

quests.instruction: Dan arrives at 4:20 PM. Cleo arrives 5 minutes after Dan. Ben arrives 10 minutes before Cleo. Ana arrives 5 minutes before Ben. Who arrives first?
quests.hint: Work out when each person arrives, starting with Dan.
quests.explanation: Cleo arrives at 4:25 PM, Ben at 4:15 PM and Ana at 4:10 PM. So Ana arrives first.
quests.funFact: Detectives use timelines to check where each person was at every moment.

quests.instruction: Train 2 leaves at 9:10 AM. Train 1 left 20 minutes before Train 2. Train 3 leaves 35 minutes after Train 1. When does Train 3 leave?
quests.hint: Find the time of Train 1 first.
quests.explanation: Train 1 left at 8:50 AM. Train 3 leaves 35 minutes after that, at 9:25 AM.
quests.funFact: Railway signal boxes once kept written logbooks of the exact time that each train passed.

quests.instruction: In a race, Tia took 12 minutes 30 seconds. Sam finished 45 seconds before Tia. Ravi finished 2 minutes 15 seconds after Sam. How long did Ravi take?
quests.hint: Find Sam's time first, then Ravi's.
quests.explanation: Sam took 12 minutes 30 seconds minus 45 seconds, which is 11 minutes 45 seconds. Ravi took 2 minutes 15 seconds longer than that, which is 14 minutes.
quests.funFact: Race results are recorded as the time that has passed since the starting signal.

quests.instruction: School ends at 3:15 PM. Leo has a 45-minute club, 25 minutes of travel each way and 1 hour 20 minutes of homework. Everything must be done by 6:30 PM. How many spare minutes does he have?
quests.hint: Add all the activities, then compare with the time available.
quests.explanation: 3:15 to 6:30 is 195 minutes. The activities take 45 + 25 + 25 + 80 = 175 minutes. 195 − 175 = 20 minutes.
quests.funFact: A good plan leaves some spare minutes, because tasks often take longer than expected.

quests.instruction: Maya wakes at 6:40 AM. Her morning routine takes 55 minutes and the walk to school takes 15 minutes. School starts at 8:00 AM. How many spare minutes does she have?
quests.hint: Find the time she arrives, then compare it with 8:00.
quests.explanation: 6:40 plus 55 minutes is 7:35, and 15 more minutes is 7:50. School starts at 8:00, so she has 10 spare minutes.
quests.funFact: A routine is easier to follow when you wake up at about the same time each day.

quests.instruction: From 4:20 PM, Nia must do three tasks. Task A takes 25 minutes and is due at 5:00. Task B takes 40 minutes and is due at 6:00. Task C takes 30 minutes and is due at 5:30. Which order meets every deadline?
quests.hint: Do the task with the earliest deadline first.
quests.explanation: A runs 4:20 to 4:45, which is before 5:00. C runs 4:45 to 5:15, which is before 5:30. B runs 5:15 to 5:55, which is before 6:00. The other orders make a task late.
quests.funFact: Doing the task with the earliest deadline first is a rule that planners and computer programs both use.

quests.instruction: A project needs 36 hours of work. A team works 4 hours a day, Monday to Friday only. If they start on a Monday, on which day do they finish?
quests.hint: How many working days are needed?
quests.explanation: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 working days. The first week gives 5 days, and 4 more days in the next week reach Thursday.
quests.funFact: Companies often measure work in person-hours, which means the number of hours that one person would take.

quests.instruction: A bus runs every 18 minutes starting at 6:00 AM. Which of these is a bus time?
quests.hint: List the bus times: 6:00, then add 18 minutes each time.
quests.explanation: The bus times are 6:00, 6:18, 6:36, 6:54 and 7:12. So 7:12 is a bus time, but 7:20 and 7:40 are not.
quests.funFact: Many bus timetables show only the first and last times, plus a gap such as every 18 minutes.

quests.instruction: How many days are there from 1 October to 31 December, counting both the first day and the last day?
quests.hint: Add the days in October, November and December.
quests.explanation: October has 31 days, November has 30 and December has 31. 31 + 30 + 31 = 92 days.
quests.funFact: The last three months of the year are often called the fourth quarter.

quests.instruction: The short hand is almost on the 4 and the long hand is on 10. A film that lasts 1 hour 40 minutes started at 2:25. How much of the film is left?
quests.hint: Read the clock first. Then find the end time of the film.
quests.explanation: The long hand on 10 means 50 minutes, and the short hand has not reached 4, so the time is 3:50. The film started at 2:25 and ends at 4:05. From 3:50 to 4:05 is 15 minutes.
quests.funFact: Nearly every country measures time in hours, minutes and seconds, and that shared system is what lets us plan together.

quests.instruction: A flight leaves City A on Friday at 10:30 PM and lasts 9 hours 15 minutes. City B is 5 hours ahead of City A. What is the local day and time in City B when it lands?
quests.hint: Find the landing time on City A's clock first, then add the time difference.
quests.explanation: 10:30 PM plus 9 hours 15 minutes is 7:45 AM on Saturday in City A. City B is 5 hours ahead, so it is 12:45 PM on Saturday there.
quests.funFact: A flight that crosses several time zones can land on a different date from the one it left on.

quests.instruction: A school play starts at 6:30 PM. The actors must be fully ready 10 minutes before the start. Putting on costumes takes 25 minutes, then make-up takes 20 minutes. What is the latest time they can begin costumes?
quests.hint: Work backward from the time they must be ready.
quests.explanation: They must be ready at 6:20 PM. Costumes and make-up take 25 + 20 = 45 minutes together. 45 minutes before 6:20 PM is 5:35 PM.
quests.funFact: Backstage, a five-minute call warns the performers that the show begins in five minutes.
